source.note: Second field report from RT365, on the value half. Read from Meridian's own code at e352bc8 in a working copy that was not modified. `measure` states the acceptance criterion, as REQ-05 and REQ-10 use the field; `priority` and `effort` are additive fields carrying our recommendation and our estimate, not a commitment on Meridian's side. Every request is `proposed`: re-statusing is the Meridian Product Owner's act, and nothing here records a decision on their behalf. Full argument, evidence and refusals in docs/REPORTS/PMO_MERIDIAN_REPORT_VALUE.md.

channel.rule: REQ-14..REQ-28 carry no issue number: filing them upstream is a human act on the RT365 owner's account (H-31), open at the time of writing. The Meridian Product Owner may ingest them from this file without waiting for issues.
channel.counterpart: RT365 Product Owner (docs/PRODUCT_OWNER.md); RT365 Program Orchestrator operates the loader (docs/PMO.md)

acceptance.proposed: written by the field repository, not yet triaged upstream
acceptance.done: on the branch with its test
acceptance.accepted: the requester said so on the issue

channel.escalation: a declined request with a written reason is a better artefact than an open one nobody intends to build; RT365 will record the decline and close its own line

requests.title: Value objects in the write API v1: business case and benefits by external id
requests.measure: An integration key with write:portfolio creates one business case and three benefits by external id; a second identical run returns 200 with zero creating writes; both appear in GET /api/v1/portfolio and in GET /api/v1/audit under the integration's name; a key without the scope is refused; a status transition requiring benefit.review is refused to a key lacking it, with a named reason.
requests.remaining: REQ-02 made delivery facts syncable (server/src/routes/v1.js:100-107); business_case and benefit are session-only (server/src/routes/portfolio.js). Measured: the RT365 loader makes 256 writes and can write no benefit.

requests.title: The benefit review is a scheduled act: an overdue realisation date reaches the agenda and the exception list
requests.measure: A benefit whose realise_on is past and whose status is still Forecast appears automatically in the next generated agenda of the board owning its project, and in an overdue list on the portfolio page and on /api/v1; recording a benefit.review removes it from both; the audit names the reviewer, the date and the actual/measured_on it was ruled against; a benefit with no realise_on is listed separately as undated rather than omitted.
requests.remaining: realise_on is written and displayed and read by nothing (server/src/portfolio.js:288; web/src/views/index.js:3534). The meetings benefits section counts Gate 4 documents, not reviews (shared/meetings.js:369-385). Depends on REQ-27 for the exception half.

requests.title: The gate cannot pass without a business case reconfirmed at that gate
requests.measure: With gate locking on, advancing a project whose case has not been reconfirmed at the gate being left is refused with a named reason; reconfirming then advancing succeeds; editing the case after reconfirmation makes the advance fail again; the audit and the gate record carry the case id, its row_version, the expected-cost and expected-benefit delta against the previous reconfirmation, and the reconfirmer; an override still requires overrideWhy.
requests.remaining: Engine.canAdvance reads outstanding evidence and unmet criteria only (shared/engine.js:338-352); staleSinceReconfirm is already computed and displayed (server/src/portfolio.js:356-372). Depends on REQ-26 for ladders longer than four gates.

requests.title: Forecast versus realised as one report, each benefit in its own unit
requests.measure: For a programme with mixed benefit units, the report shows per project the case figures and each benefit in its own unit with attainment and review age; the totals row sums money-denominated benefits only and states how many non-money benefits are excluded and in which units; a project with a case and no benefits, and one with benefits and no case, are each visible as such; the same object is served on /api/v1 and matches the page field for field; no derived currency conversion appears anywhere.
requests.remaining: Engine.valueProfile reads db.benefits only and never looks at business_case (shared/engine.js:652-680). Case money is whole units divided by 1e6 for display; benefit numbers are in their own unit and never divided (migrations 028, 008) - the two are not addable. Depends on REQ-14 or the value half stays hand-typed.

requests.title: Prioritisation reads the value, risk and capacity the product already holds
requests.measure: The ranked list shows per row: score with each input, hand rank if set, budget, expected benefit from the case (or 'no case'), a confidence flag derived from basis/reconfirmation/staleness, RAID exposure band, and FTE demand; two cut lines are drawn, one where the money envelope is exhausted and one where committed capacity is; changing a weight re-ranks, is refused below group level, and is audited with before/after; an unscored item still sorts to the bottom and is never treated as worst.
requests.remaining: Correction to RT365's earlier assessment: ranking DOES exist (migration 011; Engine.priority/prioritise, shared/engine.js:496-549; web/src/views/index.js:2713). This extends it - the fixed weighting is not displayed or adjustable, the value score never reads the case or the benefits, RAID exposure is not shown, and the only constraint line is money though Engine.capacity exists (shared/engine.js:382-400).

requests.title: Adoption per rollout wave, linked to the benefits the wave should move
requests.measure: A wave carries an adoption measure, unit, source and date, and a threshold; a wave in Live whose latest adoption is below its threshold appears in the exception list and on the next agenda; each benefit page lists its feeding waves with their adoption trend; a wave with no adoption measure reads as not measured, never as zero adoption.
requests.remaining: rollout_wave holds sequence, site, planned and actual dates and a status, and nothing about use (server/migrations/010_plant_and_sites.sql:64-77). Depends on REQ-14 for external write.

requests.title: Lessons offered as a checklist at the same gate on later projects
requests.measure: Opening the gate review on a project shows every Adopted lesson tagged to that gate number in the same programme or site, excluding the project's own; each is recorded considered or not-applicable with an optional note; the gate record and the audit keep the list and the reviewer; with no lessons tagged, the gate behaves exactly as before.
requests.remaining: lesson already carries gate_n, a group-level adoption act and lesson_relevance_idx(status, programme_id, site_id) built for exactly this query (server/migrations/024_lessons.sql) - the schema was designed for the use and the use was never built. Depends on REQ-26 for ladders longer than four gates.

requests.title: A book created before migration 036 cannot be migrated onto a programme gate ladder
requests.measure: A programme whose ladder is declared after its projects already exist can adopt that ladder without duplicating milestones and without destroying dated milestones or their evidence; a field repository's second load still makes no creating writes.
requests.remaining: Withdrawn and re-filed on 2026-09-08, the same day it was raised. As first published this said Meridian scaffolds both ladders. It does not: shared/engine.js::normaliseGateModel and server/src/wbs.js scaffold one, chosen by the programme's gateModel, and POST /api/admin/programmes has accepted that field since 036. Our loader never sent it, which is why our projects carried ten milestones where six were intended; it now does (scripts/meridian_sync.py, TC-PMO-002). What remains is the genuine gap: an existing book, created before the feature or before the declaration, has no migration path onto a ladder.

requests.title: Governance quality signals: decision latency, action ageing, gate cycle time, RAID review compliance, exception age
requests.measure: Each metric is computed from existing rows with no new field, shown per programme with a period-on-period trend, available on /api/v1, and defined in one place in the documentation with the timestamps it uses; a programme with too few closed items shows 'insufficient data' rather than a misleading number.
requests.remaining: No latency, cycle-time or ageing computation exists anywhere in shared/, server/src or web/src at e352bc8. No new data entry is required for any of the five.

requests.title: A gate criterion may cite a typed external artefact reference, not only a document link
requests.measure: A criterion carries a typed external reference with a locator and a digest supplied by the citing system; the gate record shows what was cited, by whom and when; replacing it after the gate creates a new version with supersedes lineage and leaves the old one readable; the independence rule of migration 037 still holds; Meridian records what was cited and never claims to have verified the digest.
requests.remaining: Restated after reading the code: the document model is stronger than RT365 first credited (uri required and host-checked at approval, SHA-256 locked, changing the link demotes to In review, supersedes lineage, liveness probe - migrations 014 and 020). But gate_criterion can cite only document_id (037), and uriHash hashes the URI STRING, not the artefact (server/src/routes/portfolio.js:2330,2464). Open: whether Meridian should probe such references at all, by analogy with 020.

requests.title: A value dashboard for the executive, snapshotted per reporting period
requests.measure: The page is generated from existing objects with no manual entry and prints on one sheet per programme; closing a period writes the extended snapshot (case figures, attainment, overdue-review count); reopening a closed period is refused as it is today; the page rendered from a past snapshot equals what the page showed at that close, field for field.
requests.remaining: Extends rather than replaces: report_snapshot is append-only by database rule and already carries benefits_promised, benefits_measured and benefits_met per project per period (server/migrations/009_periods.sql:42-79). Depends on REQ-17.

requests.title: Publish the field-repository loop as a reusable pattern: a real schema and a repository-agnostic review command
requests.measure: A JSON Schema for meridian-request-register/1 exists in the repository, the register validates against it in CI, the review script takes the register path and the id vocabulary as configuration, a second (fixture) field repository is reviewed end to end in a test, and the round is documented in English in one page.
requests.remaining: scripts/rt365-review.mjs parameterises --repo but hard-codes docs/requests/rt365.json and an RT365-specific id regex (M-nn, I-n, O-nn, H-nn, D-nnn, ADR-nnn, PR-nn) at lines 2-24 and 45. The string meridian-request-register/1 appears only in the register file; no schema for it exists at e352bc8.

requests.title: New: the value and learning objects must follow the configurable ladder, not the old four gates
requests.measure: On a programme with a six-gate ladder, a business case is reconfirmed at gate 6 and a lesson is tagged to gate 5; a gate number outside the programme's declared ladder is refused with a named reason; existing four-gate books are unaffected; the migration alters no stored value.
requests.remaining: Found by reading 5.10.0: business_case.reconfirmed_gate CHECK BETWEEN 1 AND 4 (migration 028) and the reconfirm route's 'Reconfirmation happens at a gate - 1 to 4' (server/src/routes/portfolio.js), lesson.gate_n CHECK BETWEEN 1 AND 4 (024), while gate_criterion.gate allows 1 TO 12 (037) and the ladder became programme data (036). RT365 runs a six-gate ladder and hits this at Gate E. Blocks REQ-16 and REQ-20 on any ladder longer than four.

requests.title: New: 'not measured' is not 'within tolerance' - an unmeasured benefit past its date must raise an exception
requests.measure: A project whose benefits are all unmeasured and whose realisation dates have passed raises an exception naming how many benefits are unmeasured and since when; the exception carries its two numbers like every other and closes only by an answer; the benefit tolerance display distinguishes 'no margin set', 'nothing measured' and 'within margin' as three different statements; a project with no benefits at all is covered by the existing uncased count and raises no duplicate exception.
requests.remaining: Found by reading 5.10.0: Engine.tolerance sets out.benefit only when at least one benefit has an attainment, and attainment is null unless baseline, target and actual are all present (shared/engine.js:611-627,646-651); sweepExceptions returns early for a project with no active tolerance (server/src/exceptions.js). Measuring and missing is therefore visible; never measuring is not. Extends the product's own principle that an unmeasured benefit is not a zero.

requests.title: New: carry the promise across the conversion - demand to project must seed the business case
requests.measure: Converting an approved demand creates a business case carrying its benefit_note and est_cost and citing the demand id; the case appears on the new project immediately; conversion is refused without a case where the programme requires one, with a named reason; converting a demand with no benefit_note still succeeds and the case is visibly a draft, never a fabricated justification.
requests.remaining: Found by reading 5.10.0: POST /demand/:id/convert copies the four scores, est_cost into budget and detail into description, drops benefit_note ('what it is FOR, in the sponsor's words', migration 011) and creates no business_case (server/src/routes/portfolio.js:1542-1582). Migration 028's own header describes the chain demand - case - benefit - review; this route is where it breaks.
